rationale: Ground truth's core blockers are: (1) generic enabler hooks only pipeline.transformer, leaking Ref2VA-only pipelines to be hooked with FL2VA coefficients (X doesn't hit this exact framing but verifies partition gating; Y outright claims this is 'correctly' handled, missing that the merged code already added the MiniMax-H3-specific enabler — but crucially Y also misses the inline comment about the missing packed_total kwarg entirely); (2) the 0.2 default vs 0.17 threshold bug — both X and Y catch this precisely with code citations; (3) offline Python example unrunnable due to undefined MODEL_ROOT — neither candidate flags this, a shared miss. The critical inline comments (missing packed_total on duplicate block call causing a TypeError, and the fake attention module missing attn_backend causing 6 test failures) are NOT mentioned by either candidate, but X's deep-dive into extractor fidelity and RoPE/residual mechanics is far more consistent with actually having traced the code that would surface such issues, while Y's review reads as more surface-level and even asserts things ship-shape that the ground truth flags as bugs. X's findings are technically deep, grounded with concrete line numbers, verified via execution/citation, and highly actionable; Y is competent but shallower, with less rigor and one unverified claim praising code that reviewers actually found buggy.
